title: Six batters made zero: what is the typical score?
description: A real innings with many zeros and two huge scores shows how far the mean and the median can be apart. Keeko doubts that dividing the team total by eleven tells the typical score.
teaching_notes: One idea: the median can be zero when more than half the values are zero, while a few big values lift the mean. Extras are not any batter's runs, so they are taken out before finding the mean. Watch for students who divide the team total, extras included, by eleven.

video_script.why: The child has met outliers and now sees a data set full of zeros, where the middle value is a zero.
video_script.substitution: The batters' runs from the book's own England innings, extras kept apart.
video_script.anchor: England's eleven batters: 19, 0, 0, 22, 158, 0, 184, 5, 0, 0, 0. Team total 407 including 19 extras.
video_script.wrong_move: Divides the team total, extras included, by eleven and calls that a typical batter. Six batters made zero, and the extras belong to no batter.
video_script.payoff_line: The median is zero runs, and the mean is thirty five point two seven runs per player.

final_answer.value: median 0 runs, mean 35.27 runs per player
final_answer.spoken: median zero runs, mean thirty five point two seven runs per player

maths_rules: sorted: 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 5, 19, 22, 158, 184; the 6th of 11 values is 0, so the median is 0
video_script.design: One idea: zeros and the median. Eleven score cards sit in the anchor; they sort on the board and the middle card lights up; the extras card sits apart.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about a real cricket match.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Eleven England batters came in, and the board shows their runs.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Six of them scored zero, and two scored over one hundred and fifty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The team total was four hundred and seven, with nineteen extras.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>We want the median and the mean runs per player.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Will the two be close together, or far apart?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, sort the scores from smallest to largest.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Six zeros come first, then five and nineteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The last three are twenty two, one hundred and fifty eight, and one hundred and eighty four.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, pick the middle score.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>There are eleven scores, so the middle one is the sixth, with five on each side.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The sixth score is a zero, so the median is zero runs.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, take out the extras, because no batter made them.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four hundred and seven take away nineteen leaves three hundred and eighty eight runs by the batters.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, share the batters' runs equally among the eleven batters.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>That is three hundred and eighty eight shared by eleven.

beats.on_screen: Answer: median 0 runs; mean ≈ 35.27 runs per player
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The median is zero runs, and the mean is thirty five point two seven runs per player.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The mean is far above the median, because two big scores pull it up.
<bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 407 ÷ 11 ≈ 37 crossed out; the extras card and the six zeros glow
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks each batter made about thirty seven runs, after sharing four hundred and seven among eleven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But that total includes nineteen extras, which no batter scored.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Also, six batters made zero, so that number is nowhere near a typical score.
